Messages.Author: Andrew Rowanbranch
Messages.Body:
Hi!

I've got a few questions regarding a few cards in the new Bloodlines
expansion.

1) If Reg Driscoll equips with a Leather Jacket, and moves it to another
vampire, does this count as that vampire equipping the Leather Jacket? In
other words, does Reg, the other vampire or both vampires untap at the end
of the turn?

2) It says on the Winnowers text that she can burn a vampire in my preys
uncontrolled region as a D action that costs X blood, where X is the number
of counters on that vampire. Does this mean that I can burn a vampire in my
preys uncontrolled region that doesn't have any blood whatsoever on it, for
the expendable cost of 0 blood?

3) If I play Withering in combat, can the target vampire use Disciplines to
prevent damage?

4) More of a "coming attractions" question, but will WW release any more
Bloodline Discipline cards? The reason for this is Marconius "special
ability" that lowers the cost of all cards that require Mytherceria by 1...
the problem being that there's but _1_ card (Darkling Trickery) that
actually costs blood.

5) Dumbass question really, but related to the one above. I feel pretty sure
that Kyasid cards don't count as Mytherceria cards, but does Marconius
ability lower the cost of these as well? (Would atleast be useful then...)

6) Example: There has been a Bribes played before votes are cast and both I
and my predator controls a Priscus. What votes count for the Bribes? Lets
say that I vote for the referendum, while my predator votes against it,
leaving the Prisci block undecided. Do I count as voting "for" the
referendum at large? What happens if I vote for (with another vampire), but
two other Prisci votes are cast against the referendum? Does my Priscus
count as voting _against_ the referendum because the block voted?

Thanks in advance
- Andrew

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <0hI28.5877$O5.1...@nntpserver.swip.net>, Andrew Rowanbranch

<rowan...@bigfoot.com> writes:
>1) If Reg Driscoll equips with a Leather Jacket, and moves it to another
>vampire, does this count as that vampire equipping the Leather Jacket?

It's "moving", not "equipping", so the other vampire doesn't get to
untap.

Reg did equip Leather Jacket (whether it's on him or not), so he can
untap.

>2) It says on the Winnowers text that she can burn a vampire in my preys
>uncontrolled region as a D action that costs X blood, where X is the number
>of counters on that vampire. Does this mean that I can burn a vampire in my
>preys uncontrolled region that doesn't have any blood whatsoever on it, for
>the expendable cost of 0 blood?

Sure.

>3) If I play Withering in combat, can the target vampire use Disciplines to
>prevent damage?

No, because the strike has already resolved at that point. (Though
damage is still being handle.)

>5) Dumbass question really, but related to the one above. I feel pretty sure
>that Kyasid cards don't count as Mytherceria cards, but does Marconius
>ability lower the cost of these as well?

Kiasyd cards don't count, no.

>6) Example: There has been a Bribes played before votes are cast and both I
>and my predator controls a Priscus. What votes count for the Bribes? Lets
>say that I vote for the referendum, while my predator votes against it,
>leaving the Prisci block undecided. Do I count as voting "for" the
>referendum at large?

Individual Prisci are counted as voting whichever way they cast their
own vote, not the way the Prisci block votes.


Also, Steal the Mind costs 1 blood, while Darkling Trickery costs 0. Still,
his point that Marconius' special is mostly useless holds. More so, if
fact, as Darkling Trickery is a great card (actually got to use the superior
today against a friend's Ravnos deck), while Steal the Mind is a little bit
more limited, and Basilisk's Touch isn't entirely helpful in the kind of
deck that you usually include Kiasyd in (i.e. you'd prefer to avoid combat,
or else end it as quickly as possible without spending too much blood). On
the other hand, Marconius has 7 points of Disciplines (and very well
distributed, at that) plus being an Archbishop with +1 hand damage at 9
capacity means that his special only really costs him half a point.
